key_insight: Trigonal selenium appears intrinsically defect tolerant because deep defect levels do not translate into strong nonradiative or radiative Shockley-Read-Hall recombination.
engineering_relevance: This suggests t-Se is a promising wide-band-gap absorber for tandem and indoor photovoltaics where defect tolerance can improve manufacturability and device stability.
method: First-principles calculations of point-defect physics in trigonal selenium
Screening a large chemically diverse defect set
Evaluating radiative and nonradiative SRH recombination across defect levels, charge states, and doping conditions
evidence_signal: Across the defect dataset, large lattice reorganizations and energy releases of at least 0.5 Eg per event strongly suppress nonradiative multiphonon recombination, and radiative capture is also too small to explain observed device losses.
watch_item: The conclusion is based on idealized defect calculations, so device performance may still depend on defect chemistry, microstructure, and processing-induced concentrations not fully captured here.
paper_title: Defect Tolerance in Trigonal Selenium Photovoltaics
